newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer, eye on Fed decision.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer, eye on Fed decision.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened firmer in quiet trade on Wednesday, helped by a stronger U.S. market and firmer Canadian dollar, with the market awaiting a rate decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve.

"I think it's more just marking them up on the back of the improvement in the U.S. market from yesterday. The Canadian dollar doing a little better as well is also helping things along, but trade has been pretty light," said one dealer with a bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.18 percent from 3.21 percent at Monday's close.
Activity was light with the Fed's rate-setting Open Market Committee expected to conclude its two-day meeting with a rate decision announcement at about 1415 EDT/1815 GMT.
The U.S. central bank was widely expected to hold rates steady, although that had not been fully priced into the Canadian money market, dealers said.
"If you don't get a Fed move this afternoon we may see some improvement in the Canadian dollar and we may improve a little bit on the back of that," the dealer said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.50 percent from 3.56 percent on Monday. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 4.01 percent from 4.06 percent.
Canadian financial markets were closed on Tuesday for the Canada Day holiday.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.35 percent, in the upper half of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
